title: Simultaneous Estimation of Partial-Transpose Moments with Active Memory Independent of the Moment Order
authors: Junxiang Huang, Xiaoyang Wang, Xiao Yuan, Yukun Zhang
abstract: We study the simultaneous estimation of partial-transpose moments $p_j(ρ_{AB})=\mathrm{Tr}[(ρ_{AB}^{T_B})^j]$, $j=2,\ldots,K$, of an unknown bipartite $n$-qubit state from independent copies under an explicit active-memory constraint. We give a sequential qubit-reuse realization of the partial-transpose permutation that uses at most $2n+1$ active qubits, independent of $K$, and estimates all moments $p_2,\ldots,p_K$ to uniform additive error $ε$ with total copy complexity $O(K\log K/ε^2)$. We also prove two converse bounds. First, any uniformly accurate simultaneous estimator requires $Ω(K/ε^2)$ copies in the worst case. Second, the same scaling holds on an explicit isospectral two-qubit negative-partial-transpose (NPT) family whose ordinary moments are constant while the partial-transpose moments vary. These results characterize the copy complexity of the partial-transpose moment hierarchy up to a logarithmic factor and extend simultaneous nonlinear-functional estimation from ordinary state powers to partial-transpose spectral data under active quantum memory independent of the target moment order.
summary: This theoretical paper characterizes the minimum number of quantum copies required to simultaneously estimate a sequence of partial-transpose moments for an unknown bipartite quantum state. By developing resource-efficient quantum circuits and proving matching lower bounds, it establishes the fundamental scaling laws for this type of nonlinear functional estimation under active memory constraints.
main_problem: The study focuses on developing efficient protocols for simultaneously estimating multiple partial-transpose moments of an unknown bipartite quantum state under strict active-memory constraints.
main_result: The authors achieve a total copy complexity scaling of $O(K \log K / \epsilon^2)$ while maintaining an active memory cost independent of the moment order $K$.
method: They employ sequential qubit-reuse quantum circuits to realize the partial-transpose permutation, comparing the achievable upper bound with established minimax lower bounds.
model_or_system: The system is a bipartite $n$-qubit quantum state $ho_{AB}$. The analysis revolves around estimating Partial-Transpose (PT) moments, which are related to entanglement measures like negativity.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an active-memory constraint where memory usage must not scale with $K$. A logarithmic gap exists between the upper and lower bounds.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by defining the PT moment hierarchy, presents an achievable quantum protocol with complexity $O(K \log K / \epsilon^2)$, and rigorously proves lower bounds ($\Omega(K/\epsilon^2)$) using hard state families to characterize the necessary resource scaling.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental resource characterizations for estimating non-local properties (like entanglement via PT moments) of quantum states, which is crucial for designing efficient quantum measurement protocols in quantum information processing.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Topological view of the PT permutation. Subsystem A follows the forward cycle and subsystem B follows the inverse cycle. The crossings are schematic routing events that are unfolded into a time-domain sequential implementation.

Fig. 2. Sequential qubit-reuse circuit for PT moments. One storage copy and one fresh transient copy interact through an ancilla-controlled routing layer; the transient register is then reset and reloaded. The active qubit count is always 2n + 1, independent of the target order K.
Fig. 3. LCSP-style coherent post-processing circuit. It illustrates the PT-LCSP construction used in Appendix E.

Fig. 4. Noiseless numerical sanity check of the sequential estimator. The upper panels compare exact PT moments with the qubit-reuse estimates, while the lower panels show residuals fluctuating around zero within the expected statistical scale. This figure is included only as a compact consistency check of the analytical identities proved in the paper.

Fig. 5. Small-scale cloud compatibility demonstration of PT-moment estimation with CDR mitigation [56]. We estimate PT moments up to order K = 5 for a three-qubit test state using dynamic circuits executed through the IBM Quantum cloud platform. Top panel: comparison between exact values (black), raw estimates (gray), and CDR-mitigated estimates (blue). Bottom panel: corresponding absolute errors with respect to the exact theory. The mitigated data show a systematic improvement over the raw estimates.
